newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end lower as small-caps dominate.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end lower as small-caps dominate.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks ended lower on Friday as small-capitalised issues dominated activity, with institutions remaining sidelined as they sought cheaper stocks elsewhere in the region, analysts said.

At the close the key Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks shed 7.30 points, or 0.68 percent, to 1,073.31. The small-capitalised Second Board index gained 2.21 points or 0.39 percent to 566.94.
"Clients would like to stay away from Malaysia at the moment because there are opportunities elsewhere," said Ken Loo, head of research at Amsteel Securities.

Thai stocks rose for the third consecutive day on Friday, gaining 38.71 points, or 6.26 percent, to 656.69. The sharp gains in Thai stocks were spurred by the country's central bank decoupling the baht from the U.S. dollar on Wednesday.

Malaysian International Shipping Corporation Bhd fell 10 cents to 7.10 ringgit. Brokers Thong & Kay Hian said in a research report on Friday that transportation firms Diperdana and Konsortium could be negotiating to buy a stake in MISC.
Volume rose to 305 million ringgit, valued at 1,750 million ringgit. Losers nudged out gainers 299 to 281.
